text.title: The Daughters of the Late Colonel
text.author: Katherine Mansfield
text.description: Two unmarried sisters, Josephine and Constantia Pinner, navigate the week following their father's death, managing practical arrangements, household staff, and unexpected visitors while grappling with complex emotions about their loss and their own futures.

josephine-pinner.name: Josephine Pinner
josephine-pinner.description: The elder of the two sisters, more practical and decisive, though prone to anxiety and emotional outbursts. She takes charge of arrangements but struggles with guilt about the burial.
josephine-pinner.context: Unmarried daughter of the late Colonel Pinner, living in a London flat with her sister

data.physicalDescription: Small red hands, pale eyebrows, bead-like eyes
Small red hands, pale eyebrows, bead-like eyes
data.transitionDescription: Josephine is awake the night after the funeral, discussing practical matters with her sister while lying in bed. She is already thinking about what to do with father's belongings.

factors.description: The funeral has just occurred; practical matters demand attention

data.physicalDescription: Small red hands, pale eyebrows, bead-like eyes
data.transitionDescription: Josephine becomes irritated with Nurse Andrews' behavior at mealtimes, particularly her excessive consumption of butter. She tries to maintain composure but shows her frustration through physical tension.

factors.description: Nurse Andrews' behavior at meals triggers Josephine's irritation
The story about the butter device adds to Josephine's frustration

data.physicalDescription: Small red hands, pale eyebrows, bead-like eyes
data.transitionDescription: Josephine experiences acute anxiety about having buried father without his permission. She imagines his anger and feels they have committed a terrible wrong. She breaks down crying.

factors.description: The moment of lowering the coffin triggers existential terror
Her imagination of father's response intensifies the guilt

data.physicalDescription: Small red hands, pale eyebrows, bead-like eyes
data.transitionDescription: Josephine is terrified entering father's room. She feels his presence in the furniture and cannot open drawers. She experiences a moment of panic where she believes father is watching from inside the chest of drawers.

factors.description: Entering the room triggers deep fear
The physical act of approaching the chest triggers her fear
Constantia's bold action allows them to leave the room

data.physicalDescription: Small red hands, pale eyebrows, bead-like eyes
data.transitionDescription: After the trauma of the room, Josephine recovers her practical nature. She makes decisions about gifts and becomes focused on Cyril's visit. She is pleased when Cyril remembers his father's preference for meringues.

factors.description: Returning to normal routines helps restore her equilibrium
Thinking of Cyril shifts her focus to the future
Cyril's correct answer about meringues pleases her

data.physicalDescription: Small red hands, pale eyebrows, bead-like eyes
data.transitionDescription: Josephine raises the question of whether to keep Kate, recognizing that everything is different now that father is gone. She is more decisive about this practical matter but also aware of the larger implications.

factors.description: The practical question forces her to confront change
Discussing independence makes her aware of new possibilities

data.physicalDescription: Small red hands, pale eyebrows, bead-like eyes
data.transitionDescription: When the barrel-organ plays, Josephine experiences a moment of strange peace. She reflects on her mother's death and wonders if their lives might have been different. She is drawn to the window by the sunlight and experiences a moment of openness to possibility.

factors.description: The barrel-organ triggers emotional release
Realizing father won't stop the organ makes her aware of freedom
The sunlight creates a moment of beauty and possibility
Memories of mother prompt reflection on what might have been

constantia-pinner.name: Constantia Pinner
constantia-pinner.description: The younger sister, more passive and dreamy than Josephine, but capable of surprising boldness. She is imaginative and sensitive, often lost in thought.
constantia-pinner.context: Unmarried daughter of the late Colonel Pinner, living in a London flat with her sister

data.physicalDescription: Long pale face, pale stare, big cold hands, long arms
Long pale face, pale stare, big cold hands, long arms
data.transitionDescription: Constantia lies in bed, thinking about the porter and his need for a top-hat. She is sensitive to others' circumstances and suggests giving him a gift.

factors.description: She notices the porter's need and suggests kindness

data.physicalDescription: Long pale face, pale stare, big cold hands, long arms
data.transitionDescription: Constantia hears a mouse and feels pity for it. She worries about how it will survive without food and wishes she had left a biscuit for it. This shows her capacity for empathy even for small things.

factors.description: The sound of the mouse triggers her empathy
Her imagination about the mouse's plight intensifies her feeling

data.physicalDescription: Long pale face, pale stare, big cold hands, long arms
data.transitionDescription: During Nurse Andrews' butter story, Constantia gazes away to imagine camels in the desert. She uses imagination to escape from uncomfortable social situations.

factors.description: Nurse Andrews' behavior triggers her escape into imagination

data.physicalDescription: Long pale face, pale stare, big cold hands, long arms
data.transitionDescription: Constantia performs a bold act by removing the key from the wardrobe, deliberately risking that father might be inside. This is described as one of only two or three times in her life she has acted so boldly. She shows a strange, callous smile.

factors.description: Josephine's fear prompts her to act
She deliberately removes the key, risking father's presence

data.physicalDescription: Long pale face, pale stare, big cold hands, long arms
data.transitionDescription: Constantia admits she has never been able to make up her mind about Kate. She suspects Kate of spying but cannot prove it. She is paralyzed by indecision.

factors.description: The question about Kate reveals her fundamental indecisiveness

data.physicalDescription: Long pale face, pale stare, big cold hands, long arms
data.transitionDescription: Constantia stands before the Buddha and experiences a moment of profound longing. She remembers times when she felt truly alive—lying on the floor in moonlight, singing by the sea. She realizes her actual life has been lived in a tunnel and that she has always been wanting something she cannot name.

factors.description: The barrel-organ triggers emotional opening
Realizing father won't stop the organ makes her aware of freedom
Standing before the Buddha triggers deep reflection
Memories of moments of true feeling intensify her yearning

colonel-pinner.name: Colonel Pinner (Father)
colonel-pinner.description: The deceased father of Josephine and Constantia. Though dead at the story's beginning, his presence dominates the narrative through the sisters' memories and fears. He was an authoritarian, impatient man who controlled his daughters' lives.
colonel-pinner.context: Deceased patriarch of the Pinner family, Anglo-Indian background

data.physicalDescription: Purple face, dark angry expression, one eye that glared, used a stick for thumping
Purple face, dark angry expression, one eye that glared, used a stick for thumping
data.transitionDescription: Colonel Pinner is dead, but his presence dominates the sisters' thoughts. They fear his judgment and anger even in death.

factors.description: His death is the central fact that structures the narrative

nurse-andrews.name: Nurse Andrews
nurse-andrews.description: The nurse who cared for Colonel Pinner during his final illness. She stays on as a guest for a week after his death, much to the sisters' discomfort. She is described as taking advantage of their kindness, particularly regarding butter.
nurse-andrews.context: Professional nurse who cared for the Colonel; stays as guest after his death

data.physicalDescription: Wears eyeglasses, has a laugh like a spoon tinkling against a medicine-glass
Wears eyeglasses, has a laugh like a spoon tinkling against a medicine-glass
data.transitionDescription: Nurse Andrews is staying with the sisters as a guest. She is kind but her presence complicates their mourning. She takes excessive butter and tells stories about her previous employers.

factors.description: Josephine invited her to stay
She accepted the invitation

mr-farolles.name: Mr. Farolles
mr-farolles.description: The vicar of St. John's church. He calls on the sisters to offer condolences and discuss funeral arrangements. He is well-meaning but somewhat obsequious and makes the sisters uncomfortable.
mr-farolles.context: Vicar of St. John's, friend of the late Colonel

data.physicalDescription: Wears kid gloves, black straw hat, glides through rooms
Wears kid gloves, black straw hat, glides through rooms
data.transitionDescription: Mr. Farolles visits to offer condolences and help. He offers communion and discusses funeral arrangements. He is formal and earnest in his approach.

factors.description: He arrives to pay his respects

kate.name: Kate
kate.description: The servant in the Pinner household. She is described as young and bold, with a somewhat dismissive attitude toward her employers. The sisters debate whether to keep her or let her go.

data.physicalDescription: Young, described as an enchanted princess
Young, described as an enchanted princess
data.transitionDescription: Kate serves meals and is described as bold and efficient. She snatches away plates and slaps down food.

factors.description: Kate is mentioned as seeing the sisters in their dressing-gowns

data.physicalDescription: Young, described as an enchanted princess
data.transitionDescription: Kate's employment is questioned by the sisters. They wonder if they can trust her and whether she spies on them. Her future with the household is uncertain.

factors.description: Her abrupt manner prompts the sisters to question her
Josephine formally raises the question of keeping her

cyril.name: Cyril
cyril.description: The grandson of Colonel Pinner, son of Benny. He lives in London and comes to tea with his aunts. He is young, somewhat forgetful, and has a good appetite despite claiming otherwise.
cyril.context: Grandson of the late Colonel, son of Benny in Ceylon

data.physicalDescription: Young man, wears waistcoats
Young man, wears waistcoats
data.transitionDescription: Cyril comes to tea with his aunts. He is polite but somewhat uncomfortable. He claims to have just eaten lunch and cannot eat much cake.

factors.description: He arrives for the visit

data.physicalDescription: Young man, wears waistcoats
data.transitionDescription: Cyril initially forgets that his father likes meringues, which embarrasses and upsets his aunts. He then corrects himself and remembers, pleasing them greatly.

factors.description: He initially cannot remember his father's preference
He remembers and corrects himself

data.physicalDescription: Young man, wears waistcoats
data.transitionDescription: Cyril visits his grandfather in his room. The visit is awkward, with the grandfather hard of hearing and Cyril having to shout about meringues. Cyril is eager to leave to meet someone at Paddington.

factors.description: He visits his grandfather as requested
The grandfather's deafness and irritability make the visit awkward

grandfather-pinner.name: Grandfather Pinner
grandfather-pinner.description: The father of Colonel Pinner, still living at the time of the story. He is elderly, hard of hearing, impatient, and irritable. He sits by a roaring fire and uses a stick for emphasis.
grandfather-pinner.context: Father of the late Colonel Pinner, elderly patriarch

data.physicalDescription: Sits by roaring fire, clasps stick, thick rug over knees, pale yellow silk handkerchief on lap
Sits by roaring fire, clasps stick, thick rug over knees, pale yellow silk handkerchief on lap
data.transitionDescription: Grandfather Pinner is hard of hearing and irritable. He demands to know what Cyril has come to tell him. He is confused by the discussion of meringues and finds it extraordinary that Cyril came to tell him about his father's preference.

factors.description: Cyril's visit triggers his irritability

benny.name: Benny
benny.description: The son of Colonel Pinner, living in Ceylon. He is not present in the story but is discussed by the sisters regarding what gift to send him. He is described as having a hand that shakes like his father's when impatient.
benny.context: Son of the late Colonel, living in Ceylon with wife Hilda

data.physicalDescription: Right hand shakes like father's when impatient
Right hand shakes like father's when impatient
data.transitionDescription: The sisters discuss what to send to Benny in Ceylon. Josephine initially thinks of sending him father's watch but then decides to send it to Cyril instead.

factors.description: The sisters begin discussing what to send Benny
Josephine changes her mind in favor of Cyril

hilda.name: Hilda
hilda.description: The wife of Benny, living in Ceylon. She is described as the unknown sister-in-law, sitting in a cane rocker reading the Tatler, not interested in the scene around her.
hilda.context: Wife of Benny, living in Ceylon

data.physicalDescription: Sits in cane rocker, reads Tatler
Sits in cane rocker, reads Tatler
data.transitionDescription: Hilda is imagined by the sisters as sitting in a cane rocker in Ceylon, reading the Tatler and not interested in family matters.

factors.description: The sisters imagine her while discussing Benny

mother-pinner.name: Mother Pinner
mother-pinner.description: The deceased mother of Josephine and Constantia. She died thirty-five years before the story begins. Her photograph hangs in the drawing room, showing her with earrings shaped like tiny pagodas and a black feather boa.
mother-pinner.context: Deceased mother of the Pinner sisters, died in Ceylon thirty-five years ago

data.physicalDescription: Photograph shows earrings shaped like tiny pagodas and black feather boa
Photograph shows earrings shaped like tiny pagodas and black feather boa
data.transitionDescription: Josephine reflects on her mother's photograph and wonders if everything would have been different if mother had not died. She considers whether they might have married if mother had lived.

factors.description: The sunlight on mother's photograph triggers reflection

aunt-florence.name: Aunt Florence
aunt-florence.description: The sister of the late Colonel Pinner. She lived with the sisters until they left school. She is mentioned only briefly as part of the sisters' history.
aunt-florence.context: Sister of the late Colonel, lived with the Pinner sisters

mr-knight.name: Mr. Knight
mr-knight.description: A funeral director mentioned by Mr. Farolles. He is described as a good friend who will help arrange the funeral.
mr-knight.context: Funeral director, friend of Mr. Farolles

lady-tukes.name: Lady Tukes
lady-tukes.description: A former employer of Nurse Andrews, mentioned in a story about a silver Cupid butter dish. She is not present in the story but is referenced to illustrate Nurse Andrews' tendency to take advantage of kindness.

pinner-flat.name: The Pinner Flat
pinner-flat.description: The London flat where Josephine and Constantia live with their father. It is a modest, respectable middle-class home with a bedroom, dining room, drawing room, kitchen, and the father's room.
pinner-flat.context: London residence of the Pinner family

data.atmosphere: Respectable, constrained, dominated by the father's presence

bedroom.name: The Sisters' Bedroom
bedroom.description: The bedroom where Josephine and Constantia sleep. They lie in separate beds, unable to sleep the night after the funeral, discussing practical matters and their feelings.
bedroom.context: Private sleeping quarters of the sisters

fathers-room.name: Father's Room
fathers-room.description: The room of the late Colonel Pinner. It is cold, white-shrouded, with blinds down, a cloth over the mirror, a sheet hiding the bed, and a huge fan of white paper in the fireplace. The sisters find it terrifying to enter.
fathers-room.context: Bedroom of the late Colonel Pinner

data.atmosphere: Terrifying, cold, white, haunted by father's presence

dining-room.name: The Dining Room
dining-room.description: The dining room of the flat where the sisters eat meals with Nurse Andrews. It is where they discuss practical matters and where they later retire to discuss Kate.
dining-room.context: Eating and discussion space in the flat

data.atmosphere: Functional, tense with Nurse Andrews present, later reflective

drawing-room.name: The Drawing Room
drawing-room.description: The formal drawing room of the flat where Mr. Farolles is received and where the sisters retire to discuss Kate. It contains a piano, a mantelpiece with a Buddha statue, and photographs including one of their mother.
drawing-room.context: Formal reception and discussion space in the flat

data.atmosphere: Formal, reflective, containing memories and art

kitchen.name: The Kitchen
kitchen.description: The kitchen of the flat where Kate works. It is mentioned as the place where Kate prepares meals and where the sisters might ask her for things.
kitchen.context: Working space of the servant Kate

cemetery.name: The Cemetery
cemetery.description: The cemetery where Colonel Pinner is buried. Josephine experiences acute anxiety here as the coffin is lowered, realizing they have buried their father without his permission.

cab.name: The Cab from the Cemetery
cab.description: The cab in which Josephine and Constantia travel from the cemetery. Josephine breaks down crying in the cab, expressing her guilt about the burial.

grandfathers-room.name: Grandfather's Room
grandfathers-room.description: The room of Grandfather Pinner, where Cyril visits him. It is hot and sweetish, with a roaring fire, and the grandfather sits with a thick rug over his knees.

data.atmosphere: Hot, stifling, dominated by grandfather's irritability

ceylon.name: Ceylon
ceylon.description: The location where Benny lives with his wife Hilda. It is imagined by the sisters as a place with hot climate, runners instead of post, and veranda life. It is also where their mother died thirty-five years ago.
ceylon.context: Colonial location where Benny lives; where mother died

eastbourne.name: Eastbourne
eastbourne.description: A seaside resort where the sisters stayed at a boarding house. A mysterious man left a note on the jug of hot water outside their bedroom door, but the writing was too faint to read.
eastbourne.context: Seaside resort visited by the sisters

london-street.name: London Street Below the Flat
london-street.description: The street below the flat where a barrel-organ plays. The sound of the barrel-organ triggers the sisters' emotional release at the end of the story.

desert-imagined.name: Desert (Imagined)
desert-imagined.description: An imagined desert landscape that Constantia visualizes while uncomfortable at mealtimes. She imagines a line of camels unwinding like a thread of wool.

sea-imagined.name: The Sea (Remembered)
sea-imagined.description: The sea that Constantia remembers visiting and where she would sing and feel truly alive. It represents a moment of authentic feeling and freedom.

top-hat.name: Father's Top-Hat
top-hat.description: The top-hat of the late Colonel Pinner. Constantia suggests giving it to the porter, who she noticed only had a bowler at the cemetery.
top-hat.context: Formal headwear of the late Colonel

bowler-hat-porter.name: Porter's Bowler Hat
bowler-hat-porter.description: The bowler hat worn by the porter at the cemetery. Constantia notices he only has this and suggests giving him the father's top-hat.
bowler-hat-porter.context: Hat worn by the cemetery porter

dressing-gown-josephine.name: Josephine's Dressing-Gown
dressing-gown-josephine.description: Josephine's dressing-gown, which is dark-red and matches her slippers. The sisters discuss whether they should dye their dressing-gowns black for mourning.

dressing-gown-constantia.name: Constantia's Dressing-Gown
dressing-gown-constantia.description: Constantia's dressing-gown, which is indefinite green and matches her slippers. The sisters discuss whether they should dye their dressing-gowns black for mourning.
dressing-gown-constantia.physicalDescription: Indefinite green dressing-gown with matching slippers

mourning-handkerchief.name: Josephine's Mourning Handkerchief
mourning-handkerchief.description: A new, queer-smelling mourning handkerchief that Josephine uses to cry into. It is described as new and having an unusual smell.

blotting-paper.name: Blotting-Paper
blotting-paper.description: Blotting-paper used by Josephine to soak up tears while writing condolence replies. She used it on some of the twenty-three letters she wrote.

sheet-covering-bed.name: Sheet Covering the Bed
sheet-covering-bed.description: A white sheet that covers the bed in father's room. It is part of the white-shrouded appearance of the room.

cloth-mirror.name: Cloth Over the Mirror
cloth-mirror.description: A cloth hung over the mirror in father's room as part of mourning customs.

fan-fireplace.name: Fan of White Paper
fan-fireplace.description: A huge fan of white paper that fills the fireplace in father's room. It is part of the white-shrouded appearance of the room.

blind.name: Blind in Father's Room
blind.description: The blind in father's room that is pulled down. When the sisters touch it, it flies up suddenly, startling them.

chest-of-drawers.name: Chest of Drawers
chest-of-drawers.description: The chest of drawers in father's room where Josephine fears father is hiding. She imagines he is in the top drawer with his handkerchiefs and neckties, or in the next with his shirts and pyjamas, or in the lowest with his suits.
chest-of-drawers.physicalDescription: Chest of drawers with multiple drawers

wardrobe.name: Wardrobe
wardrobe.description: A huge glittering wardrobe in father's room. Constantia boldly removes the key from it, risking that father might be inside among his overcoats.
wardrobe.culturalSignificance: Object of fear and Constantia's bold action

writing-table.name: Locked Writing-Table
writing-table.description: A locked writing-table in father's room that the sisters do not open. Constantia notes it as safe.

hot-water-cups.name: Cups of Hot Water
hot-water-cups.description: Two cups of hot water that Josephine and Constantia ask Kate to bring them after leaving father's room. They drink from them to recover from their ordeal.

fathers-watch.name: Father's Gold Watch
fathers-watch.description: The gold watch of the late Colonel Pinner. Josephine initially considers sending it to Benny in Ceylon but ultimately decides to give it to Cyril.
fathers-watch.context: Valuable possession of the late Colonel
fathers-watch.culturalSignificance: Symbol of inheritance and family connection

corset-box.name: Cardboard Corset-Box
corset-box.description: A narrow cardboard corset-box with lettering 'Medium Women's 28. Extra Firm Busks' that Josephine considers using to disguise the watch. She decides against it as inappropriate.
corset-box.context: Household item considered for gift packaging

cakes-buszards.name: Cakes from Buszard's
cakes-buszards.description: Rich dark cakes purchased from Buszard's for Cyril's visit. Josephine describes them as standing for her winter gloves or the soling and heeling of Constantia's shoes.

meringues.name: Meringues
meringues.description: Meringues purchased specially for Cyril's visit. They are significant because Josephine and Constantia believe Cyril's father (Benny) is fond of them, and later Cyril's grandfather is confused by the discussion of meringues.
meringues.culturalSignificance: Symbol of family connection and memory

chocolate-roll.name: Chocolate-Roll
chocolate-roll.description: A chocolate-roll offered to Cyril during his visit. Constantia sits with her knife poised over it.

blancmange.name: Blancmange
blancmange.description: A white, terrified blancmange served by Kate. It is described as mock something or other, and the sisters consider serving it with jam or marmalade.

jam-pot.name: Jam-Pot
jam-pot.description: An empty jam-pot that Kate brings to the table. It is empty, causing the sisters to look for marmalade instead.

marmalade.name: Marmalade
marmalade.description: Marmalade found in the sideboard as a substitute for jam. Nurse Andrews hopes it is not very bitter.

butter-dish-lady-tukes.name: Silver Cupid Butter Dish
butter-dish-lady-tukes.description: A silver Cupid balanced on the border of a glass dish, holding a tiny fork, used for serving butter. Nurse Andrews describes it from her time with Lady Tukes. When you wanted butter, you pressed the Cupid's foot and he bent down and speared a piece.
butter-dish-lady-tukes.context: Luxury item from Nurse Andrews' past employment
butter-dish-lady-tukes.physicalDescription: Silver Cupid balanced on border of glass dish, holding tiny fork

stick-father.name: Father's Stick
stick-father.description: The stick used by Colonel Pinner for thumping. It is mentioned as something that will never thump again after his death.
stick-father.culturalSignificance: Symbol of father's authority and control

barrel-organ.name: Barrel-Organ
barrel-organ.description: A barrel-organ that plays in the street below the flat. It plays music that seems to comment on the sisters' situation, including 'A week since father died' and 'It never will thump again.'
barrel-organ.culturalSignificance: Catalyst for emotional release and reflection

buddha-statue.name: Buddha Statue
buddha-statue.description: A stone and gilt Buddha statue on the mantelpiece in the drawing room. It has a smile that gives Constantia a queer feeling, almost a pain and yet a pleasant pain. She feels it knows something she doesn't.
buddha-statue.context: Decorative object in the drawing room
buddha-statue.culturalSignificance: Symbol of mystery and spiritual knowledge

mothers-photograph.name: Mother's Photograph
mothers-photograph.description: An enlargement of the mother's photograph hanging over the piano in the drawing room. It is thirty-five years old and shows her with earrings shaped like tiny pagodas and a black feather boa. The photograph has faded significantly.
mothers-photograph.context: Family photograph in the drawing room
mothers-photograph.physicalDescription: Enlargement showing mother with pagoda earrings and black feather boa
mothers-photograph.culturalSignificance: Symbol of lost mother and past

indian-carpet.name: Indian Carpet
indian-carpet.description: An Indian carpet in the drawing room on which sunlight falls, creating a square of pale red light.
indian-carpet.context: Floor covering in the drawing room

piano.name: Piano
piano.description: A piano in the drawing room over which mother's photograph hangs. The sisters consider it too high for Mr. Farolles to lean over with the chalice during communion.
piano.context: Musical instrument in the drawing room

bell.name: Bell
bell.description: A bell in the flat that might ring during communion, interrupting the service. The sisters worry about this possibility.

amethyst-cross.name: Amethyst Cross
amethyst-cross.description: An amethyst cross belonging to Constantia. She suspects Kate of moving it when she and Josephine are out, finding it in unlikely places like under her lace ties or on top of her evening Bertha.

lace-ties.name: Lace Ties
lace-ties.description: Lace ties belonging to Constantia. She finds her amethyst cross under them, suggesting Kate has been moving her things.

evening-bertha.name: Evening Bertha
evening-bertha.description: An evening Bertha (a type of shawl or collar) belonging to Constantia. She finds her amethyst cross on top of it, suggesting Kate has been moving her things.

tatler-magazine.name: Tatler Magazine
tatler-magazine.description: The Tatler magazine that Hilda is imagined reading while sitting in a cane rocker in Ceylon.

cane-rocker.name: Cane Rocker
cane-rocker.description: A cane rocker in which Hilda is imagined sitting in Ceylon while reading the Tatler.

veranda.name: Veranda
veranda.description: The veranda in Ceylon where Benny is imagined standing, dressed all in white and wearing a cork helmet, his right hand shaking like father's when impatient.

cork-helmet.name: Cork Helmet
cork-helmet.description: A cork helmet worn by Benny in the imagined scene in Ceylon.

note-on-jug.name: Note on the Jug
note-on-jug.description: A mysterious note left by a man on the jug of hot water outside the sisters' bedroom door at Eastbourne. The writing was too faint to read due to steam.

carved-screen.name: Carved Screen
carved-screen.description: A carved screen with horrible dancing figures that Constantia remembers from lying on the floor in moonlight. The figures leered at her but she didn't mind.
carved-screen.culturalSignificance: Associated with Constantia's moments of authentic feeling

moon.name: Moon
moon.description: The full moon that Constantia remembers lying under, which made her lie on the floor with her arms outstretched as though crucified.
moon.culturalSignificance: Symbol of authentic feeling and spiritual experience

sunlight.name: Sunlight
sunlight.description: Sunlight that enters the drawing room through the windows, creating a square of pale red light on the Indian carpet that deepens to golden. It triggers the sisters' emotional release.
sunlight.context: Natural light in the drawing room
sunlight.physicalDescription: Pale red light that deepens to golden

e01-josephine-asks-about-top-hat.description: Josephine asks Constantia if she thinks father would mind if they gave his top-hat to the porter.

e02-constantia-suggests-porter.description: Constantia explains that the porter must often have to go to funerals and she noticed at the cemetery that he only had a bowler. She suggests they ought to give him a present.

e03-josephine-nearly-giggles.description: Josephine nearly giggles at the image of the porter's head disappearing and popping out like a candle under father's hat. She fights down the giggle and tells herself to remember.

e04-discussion-of-dressing-gowns.description: Constantia asks if they ought to have their dressing-gowns dyed black as well. Josephine is shocked at the suggestion. They discuss whether it's necessary to wear black at home.

e05-kate-mentioned.description: Constantia mentions that Kate sees them in their dressing-gowns, and the postman might also see them. This is part of the discussion about whether to dye their dressing-gowns black.

e06-letters-discussion.description: Constantia asks how many letters they have had. Josephine replies twenty-three. She has replied to them all, breaking down each time she wrote 'We miss our dear father so much.'

e07-mouse-sound.description: There comes a little rustle, scurry, and hop. Constantia says it's a mouse.

e08-constantia-pities-mouse.description: Constantia feels pity for the mouse, wishing she had left a tiny piece of biscuit on the dressing-table. She worries about how it will survive without finding anything.

e09-josephine-dismisses-mouse-talk.description: Josephine is furious at Constantia's concern for mice, saying 'Oh, what nonsense, Con!' and accusing her of being asleep. Constantia closes her eyes to check if she is asleep.

e10-josephine-suggests-nurse-andrews.description: Josephine suggests to Constantia that they ask Nurse Andrews to stay on for a week as their guest after the doctor has gone. Constantia agrees it would be very nice.

e11-nurse-andrews-accepts.description: Nurse Andrews jumps at the idea of staying on as a guest for a week.

e12-meal-time-butter-incident.description: Nurse Andrews is fearful about butter at mealtimes, taking excessive amounts. Josephine gets very red and stares at the tablecloth. Constantia gazes away to the desert imagining camels.

e13-nurse-andrews-story-about-lady-tukes.description: Nurse Andrews tells a story about Lady Tukes' silver Cupid butter dish that would dispense butter when you pressed the Cupid's foot. Josephine finds this story unbearable.

e14-jam-pot-empty.description: Kate brings an empty jam-pot to the table. The sisters realize there is no jam and must find an alternative.

e15-marmalade-solution.description: Josephine suggests using marmalade instead of jam. She asks Constantia to get it from the sideboard. Nurse Andrews hopes it is not very bitter.

e16-reflection-on-nurse-kindness.description: The narrator reflects that Nurse Andrews had been very kind to father, nursing him day and night at the end, though the sisters felt she had overdone it by not leaving him at the very last.

e17-father-death-scene-memory.description: The sisters remember going in to say goodbye to father. He lay there purple and angry, never looking at them. Then he suddenly opened one eye, glared at them, and it went out. The sisters wish he had opened both eyes.

e18-mr-farolles-arrives.description: Mr. Farolles, the vicar of St. John's, calls on the sisters the same afternoon. He glides towards them through the dark drawing-room.

e19-farolles-offers-communion.description: Mr. Farolles offers to give the sisters a little Communion, either or both of them, here and now. The idea terrifies them as they imagine the practical difficulties.

e20-sisters-decline-communion.description: The sisters decline the offer of immediate Communion, saying they might send a note later if they would care for it.

e21-farolles-discusses-funeral.description: Mr. Farolles asks if he may arrange the funeral as their dear father's old friend. He takes his black straw hat from the round table.

e22-josephine-requests-simplicity.description: Josephine says she would like the funeral to be quite simple and not too expensive, but suitable to their father's position. She is very nervous.

e23-farolles-mentions-mr-knight.description: Mr. Farolles says he will run round to their good friend Mr. Knight, the funeral director, and ask him to come see them.

e24-josephine-terror-at-cemetery.description: At the cemetery, while the coffin is lowered, Josephine experiences absolute terror, thinking that she and Constantia have done this thing without asking father's permission. She imagines his anger.

e25-josephine-imagines-fathers-anger.description: Josephine imagines father roaring 'And do you expect me to pay for this gimcrack excursion of yours?' She feels they should not have done it.

e26-josephine-breaks-down.description: Josephine breaks down and cries into her new, queer-smelling mourning handkerchief. She says 'we shouldn't have done it, Con!'

e27-constantia-questions-alternatives.description: Constantia asks what else they could have done. She points out they couldn't have kept father unburied in a flat that size.

e28-josephine-fears-fathers-forgiveness.description: Josephine says 'father will never forgive us for this—never!' She feels certain of this and her tears spring out again.

e29-sisters-approach-fathers-room.description: Two mornings later, the sisters go into father's room to go through his things. It is dark in the hall. Josephine pushes Constantia to go first, but Constantia says it's not fair as Josephine is the eldest.

e30-josephine-pushes-constantia.description: Josephine pushes Constantia toward the door, saying 'You—you go first' in a gasp.

e31-room-description-white-covered.description: The sisters enter father's room. Everything is covered in white. The blinds are down, a cloth hangs over the mirror, a sheet hides the bed, and a huge fan of white paper fills the fireplace. The room is cold.

e32-blind-pulled-up.description: Josephine pulls up the blind. It flies up suddenly and the cord rolls round the blind-stick, with the tassel tapping as if trying to get free. This startles Constantia.

e33-josephine-fears-father-in-drawers.description: Josephine approaches the chest of drawers but quickly draws her hand back. She has an extraordinary feeling that she has just escaped something awful. She imagines father is in the chest of drawers, hidden away, ready to spring.

e34-constantia-removes-wardrobe-key.description: Constantia performs a bold act. She marches over to the wardrobe, turns the key, and takes it out of the lock. She holds it up to Josephine with an extraordinary smile, showing she knows she has risked father being in there among his overcoats.

e35-sisters-return-to-dining-room.description: The sisters return to the dining room, very shaky. They sit down and look at each other.

e36-josephine-asks-for-hot-water.description: Josephine says she doesn't feel she can settle to anything until she's had something. She asks if they could ask Kate for two cups of hot water.

e37-benny-discussion-begins.description: Josephine mentions Benny and says he'll expect them to send him something of father's. She notes it's difficult to know what to send to Ceylon. Constantia mentions things get unstuck on the voyage. Josephine corrects her, saying things get lost.

e38-josephine-decides-on-watch.description: Josephine says she thinks father's watch would be the most suitable present for Benny.

e39-constantia-questions-native-trust.description: Constantia asks if Josephine would trust a gold watch to a native. Josephine says of course she would disguise it so no one would know it was a watch.

e40-josephine-plans-disguise.description: Josephine thinks of disguising the watch in a narrow cardboard corset-box with lettering 'Medium Women's 28. Extra Firm Busks.' She decides against it as inappropriate for the occasion.

e41-josephine-thinks-of-cyril.description: Josephine suddenly thinks of Cyril. She wonders if it's more usual for the only grandson to have the watch. She notes that Cyril is appreciative and a gold watch means much to a young man.

e42-josephine-prefers-cyril.description: Josephine decides it would be nice for her and Constantia to know the watch is with Cyril when he comes to tea. She imagines saying 'I see you've got on grandfather's watch, Cyril.'

e43-cyril-visit-anticipated.description: The narrator notes that Cyril had sent a sweet, sympathetic note, but it was most unfortunate that he couldn't come to the funeral. However, he will come to tea with his aunties soon, which is one of their rare treats.

e44-cyril-arrives-for-tea.description: Cyril arrives for tea with his aunties. Josephine tells him not to be frightened of their cakes, which they bought at Buszard's. She cuts recklessly into the rich dark cake.

e45-cyril-refuses-cake.description: Cyril says he simply can't eat cake because he's only just had lunch. Josephine is disappointed, noting it's after four. Cyril explains he had to meet a man at Victoria who kept him hanging about.

e46-meringue-discussion.description: Josephine asks if Cyril will have a meringue, saying they were bought specially for him because his dear father was so fond of them. Cyril eagerly agrees and asks if he can take half to begin with.

e47-cyril-forgets-fathers-preference.description: Constantia asks if Cyril's dear father is still so fond of meringues. Cyril says he doesn't quite know. Josephine and Constantia are shocked that he doesn't know this about his own father.

e48-cyril-corrects-himself.description: Cyril suddenly remembers and says 'Of course, it was meringues. How could I have forgotten? Yes, Aunt Josephine, you're perfectly right. Father's most frightfully keen on meringues.' Josephine goes scarlet with pleasure and Constantia gives a deep sigh.

e49-cyril-visits-grandfather.description: Josephine says Cyril must come and see father (grandfather). Cyril agrees firmly and heartily, but then glances at the clock and says he has to meet a man at Paddington just after five and won't be able to stay very long.

e50-grandfather-pinner-scene.description: The sisters and Cyril knock at the door and enter grandfather's hot, sweetish room. Grandfather Pinner is sitting in front of a roaring fire, clasping his stick, with a thick rug over his knees and a pale yellow silk handkerchief on his lap.

e51-meringues-conversation-with-grandfat.description: Grandfather Pinner is hard of hearing. Josephine tries to tell him that Cyril says his father is still very fond of meringues. The grandfather can't hear and makes Cyril shout about meringues. He finds it extraordinary that Cyril came all this way to tell him about meringues.

e52-josephine-decides-cyril-gets-watch.description: After the visit, Josephine says 'Yes, I shall send Cyril the watch.' Constantia agrees it would be very nice, noting there was some little trouble about the time last time he came.

e53-kate-asks-fried-or-boiled.description: Kate bursts through the door asking 'Fried or boiled?' The sisters are bewildered. Josephine asks 'Fried or boiled what, Kate?' Kate sniffs and says 'Fish.'

e54-sisters-confused.description: Josephine and Constantia are quite bewildered by Kate's abrupt question. They can hardly take it in.

e55-kate-means-fish.description: Kate clarifies that she's asking about fish. Josephine gently reproaches her for not saying so immediately, noting there are many things in the world that are fried or boiled.

e56-sisters-retire-to-drawing-room.description: Josephine asks Constantia to follow her into the drawing-room, saying she has something of great importance to discuss. They retire to the drawing-room to talk over Kate.

e57-josephine-raises-kate-question.description: Josephine asks Constantia if they shall keep Kate or not. She says this time they must come to a definite decision. She notes that everything is so changed now—there's not father to cook for.

e58-discussion-of-independence.description: Josephine explains that they're not dependent on Kate as they were. They could manage their own food if they gave Kate notice. She suggests they could live on eggs in various forms and cooked foods.

e59-constantia-cannot-decide-about-kate.description: Constantia says she has never been able to quite make up her mind about Kate. She suspects Kate of spying and moving her things, but can never prove it. She has laid traps but can never get proof.

e60-josephine-warns-against-postponement.description: Josephine says 'Well, we can't postpone it again. If we postpone it this time—' but is interrupted by the barrel-organ starting to play.

e61-barrel-organ-starts.description: A barrel-organ strikes up in the street below. Josephine and Constantia spring to their feet together, remembering they used to have to stop the organ-grinder.

e62-sisters-remember-father-wont-stop-it.description: The sisters remember that they will never have to stop the organ-grinder again. The stick will never thump again. The barrel-organ seems to play 'It never will thump again' and 'A week since father died.'

e63-constantia-notes-week-has-passed.description: Constantia softly says to Josephine 'Do you know what day it is? It's Saturday. It's a week to-day, a whole week.' She presses her hands together.

e64-sunlight-enters-room.description: On the Indian carpet there falls a square of sunlight, pale red. It comes and goes and comes—and stays, deepens—until it shines almost golden.

e65-josephine-comments-on-sun.description: Josephine says 'The sun's out' as though it really matters.

e66-constantia-approaches-buddha.description: Constantia lifts her big, cold hands as if to catch the bubbling notes from the barrel-organ, then her hands fall. She walks over to the mantelpiece to her favourite Buddha.

e67-josephine-watches-sunlight.description: Josephine watches the sunlight as it presses through the windows, thieving its way in, flashing its light over the furniture and photographs.

e68-josephine-remembers-mother.description: When the sunlight comes to mother's photograph, Josephine wonders why photographs of dead people always fade so. She remembers the photograph is thirty-five years old and shows mother with earrings shaped like tiny pagodas and a black feather boa. She wonders if everything would have been different if mother hadn't died.

e69-josephine-reflects-on-marriage.description: Josephine reflects on whether she and Constantia might have married if mother had lived. She notes there had been father's Anglo-Indian friends before he quarrelled with them, but after that they never met a single man except clergymen. She remembers one year at Eastbourne when a mysterious man left a note on the jug of hot water outside their bedroom door, but the writing was too faint to read.

e70-constantia-remembers-moonlight-momen.description: Constantia remembers times when she came into the drawing room and crept out of bed in her nightgown when the moon was full, lying on the floor with her arms outstretched as though crucified. She also remembers going to the seaside and getting as close to the sea as she could, singing something she had made up. She realizes her actual life has been lived in a tunnel and that she only felt truly alive in these moments.

e71-constantia-wants-to-speak.description: Constantia turns away from the Buddha and goes over to where Josephine is standing. She wants to say something to Josephine, something frightfully important, about the future and what.

e72-both-forget-what-to-say.description: Both sisters begin to speak but interrupt each other. They wait for each other to speak. Constantia says she can't say what she was going to say because she's forgotten what it was. Josephine replies shortly that she's forgotten too.

rel-josephine-constantia.description: Josephine and Constantia are unmarried sisters living together. Josephine is the elder and more practical, while Constantia is younger and more dreamy. They are deeply dependent on each other and navigate their father's death together.
rel-josephine-constantia.nature: Sisters bound by family obligation, shared history, and mutual dependence. Josephine is more decisive and controlling; Constantia is more passive and imaginative. They complete each other but also frustrate each other.
